message.content: {"reasoning": "The reference diagnosis is a migrated plastic biliary stent that caused a perforation in the ileum, with the stent lodged in a Meckel diverticulum and inflaming it (diverticulitis). The proposed diagnosis names the same cause: a migrated plastic biliary stent acting as an intraluminal foreign body. It also names the same complication: peritonitis, with stent-related bowel perforation suspected. It does not mention the Meckel diverticulum or the diverticulitis. It also leads with small bowel obstruction, which is not part of the reference diagnosis, and it calls the perforation only suspected. These are gaps in anatomical detail and certainty rather than contradictions, because a stent lodged in the distal ileum, with perforation and peritonitis, can look like or cause obstruction. Since the proposed diagnosis captures the unusual central mechanism (biliary stent migration leading to bowel perforation and peritonitis) and nothing in it conflicts with the reference, it substantially meets the matching criterion.", "decision": true}
